note: Triennial election of the fourteen district electoral divisions of Ballycastle rural district, one member each. Nominations were lodged on 7 May 1924: four divisions were contested and the other ten were unopposed returns (Belfast News-Letter, 9 May 1924). The four contests were polled on Thursday 5 June and declared on 6 June. The fourteenth division, Dunseverick, is omitted: the candidate's surname is cut off in the only printed list traced (James M'N...), and is not guessed. Sole nomination (Nationalist); retiring member. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of the Belfast News-Letter, 9 May 1924, p. 2 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the citation now names the page that prints Frank M'Carry's nomination, the list the check already named (was the News-Letter of 7 May 1924, p. 3, which does not print it). Renamed from 'Fair Head' to The Fair Head (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Ballycastle Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED The Fair Head; the rounds were filed as Fair Head (1924, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1949); Fairhead (1946, 1955). This round was filed as 'Fair Head', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (fair-head) answers with a redirect to this one.
